title: Dragon's Lair
build: Software Projects disk, alternate D64 with LA–LJ files

records.c: The first copied byte in the scene record is $03. The caller starts executing one byte later.
Save and reload the caller stack pointer, copy the score digits, set up screen and colour pointers, use sound request $87 and initialize expanded sprite 1 before applying the scene colour lookup.
Restore the saved stack pointer, copy the digit characters and initialize score pointers. Select the room sprite configuration and start sound $87 before switching the VIC bank.
Set sprite 1 to X=$9F and Y=$34. Expand it in both directions, put it behind the background and select its colour 7 before applying the room colour table.

Save the expected action in $10 and read the joystick with active-low bits inverted. Return the expected mask on an exact match. No input returns $FF. An incorrect nonzero mask also requests sound $89 and starts a 20-call cooldown.
Update sprite 2 on expiry of $31A4. Add the two velocity bytes, toggle the high X bit on a low-byte wrap and change its vertical behaviour at the $E0 threshold.
Repeat the timed joystick and sprite updates using the initial count in A. Update the weapon-room animation on each iteration.
Wait through two CIA2 timer intervals, poll the joystick and apply the sprite cycle update. Repeat with the count in A saved to $2EC6.
Every three calls advance $31A2 down through 2, 1, 0 and write pointer $BA plus that index to sprite 1.
Use the shared 90-byte record index at $3200. Wait for the lower raster and copy the record to the zero-page sprite work area.
Use the animation index in A to look up sprite 0 coordinates and expansion bits. Set pointer $A9, enable the sprite and load the neighbouring sprite state from the same indexed family.
This scene record ends with the eleven byte marker copied by the unpacker at $0DDE.
The first page of the screen matrix for the background in VIC bank $4000. Its character codes index the scene colour lookup when the display is initialized.
Screen matrix offsets $100–$1FF. The VIC reads these as character codes and the palette routine processes a page at a time.
Screen matrix offsets $200–$2FF. The screen maps into the glyph data at $7800.
The last page of the screen matrix, including the hardware sprite pointers at $43F8–$43FF.
The two sprite fragments before the active player pair at $4480.
Two 64-byte sprite images for hardware sprites 5 and 6 at the Weapons Room capture.
Four individual sprite shapes between the active player pair and the colour table.
Table indexed by the room screen cells when the scene patches $167A to $46 and calls the shared colour routine.
Sixteen 64-byte rendered fragments including torso, hand and bent-leg graphics.
Animation parts with compact head and foot shapes in the low slots and angled limbs in the high slots.
Sixteen mask fragments immediately before the row of compact leaning poses.
Middle mask set for the player animation with varied angles of legs and armour.
Another set of adjacent sprite fragments showing outlines of boots and legs.
Sprite parts in the $6C–$7B pointer range, including the separate pair of straight lower legs.
Sixty-four-byte sprite pieces for mixed arm, head, and body animation frames.
Rendered bank of fragments continuing the player motion set, including pointed foot and knee shapes.
The 16 sprite records around the pointer $A9 selected for sprite 0 in the later room routine.
Upper range of sprite masks before the expanded sprite, including a circular weapon silhouette at pointer $B8.
The 64-byte image record selected by sprite 1 at the Weapons Room capture. Both expansion bits are set during initialization.
Seven 64-byte slots with separate shapes such as a circular disk, star and fragments of weapons. The code writes pointer $C0 to sprite 2.
The unpacked picture stream initializes $7100–$73FF to zero. These bytes are still zero in the play capture.
The scene character glyph store for VIC bank $4000 and character-base bits 3–1 of $D018 set to 7. A character occupies eight consecutive bytes.
The top half of this scene set, from character code $80. The eight-byte glyph slots are used for the scene-specific objects and screen details.
Repeated $04 bytes at $B617–$B70F, after the input consumed by the scene picture decode.
